claim: Goku was born with the Saiyan name Kakarot.
explanation: True. Goku's birth name is Kakarot, revealed in Dragon Ball Z when Raditz arrives on Earth. (Spoiler: early Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Goku was born on Earth.
explanation: False. Goku was born on Planet Vegeta and sent to Earth as a baby. (Spoiler: early Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Vegeta is the prince of the Saiyan race.
explanation: True. Vegeta is the Prince of all Saiyans, son of King Vegeta.

claim: Piccolo is a Saiyan.
explanation: False. Piccolo is a Namekian, a member of the green-skinned race from the planet Namek.

claim: Gohan is Goku's first son.
explanation: True. Gohan is the elder son of Goku and Chi-Chi; Goten is the younger.

claim: Krillin is married to Bulma.
explanation: False. Krillin is married to Android 18. Bulma is married to Vegeta.

claim: Bulma is the daughter of Dr. Brief, the founder of Capsule Corporation.
explanation: True. Bulma is the daughter of Dr. Brief and heir to Capsule Corporation.

claim: Master Roshi's Kame House stands on top of a mountain.
explanation: False. Kame House is a small house on a tiny island in the sea.

claim: Trunks is the son of Vegeta and Bulma.
explanation: True. Trunks is the son of Vegeta and Bulma.

claim: Goten is the son of Vegeta.
explanation: False. Goten is the younger son of Goku and Chi-Chi.

claim: Android 18 has a twin brother who is Android 17.
explanation: True. Androids 17 and 18 are siblings created by Dr. Gero. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Tien Shinhan is known for having a third eye on his forehead.
explanation: True. Tien is a triclops with a third eye.

claim: The Kamehameha is Goku's signature energy attack.
explanation: True. The Kamehameha is the technique most associated with Goku.

claim: Goku first becomes a Super Saiyan while fighting Cell.
explanation: False. Goku first becomes a Super Saiyan while fighting Frieza on Namek. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z, Frieza Saga.)

claim: Master Roshi is known as the Dragon Hermit.
explanation: False. Master Roshi is known as the Turtle Hermit.

claim: Bardock is Goku's father.
explanation: True. Bardock is the father of Goku and Raditz. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Raditz is Goku's cousin.
explanation: False. Raditz is Goku's older brother. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Vegeta first arrives on Earth with Nappa during the Saiyan Saga of Dragon Ball Z.
explanation: True. Vegeta and Nappa arrive to search for the Dragon Balls. (Spoiler.)

claim: Frieza destroyed Planet Vegeta.
explanation: True. Frieza destroyed the Saiyan home planet. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z backstory.)

claim: Gohan first becomes a Super Saiyan while fighting Frieza.
explanation: False. Gohan first becomes a Super Saiyan in the Cell Games arc. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Piccolo is the reincarnation of King Piccolo.
explanation: True. Piccolo was born just before King Piccolo's death and carries his legacy. (Spoiler.)

claim: Piccolo was born on the planet Namek.
explanation: False. Piccolo was born on Earth, though he is a Namekian by race.

claim: Piccolo trains the young Gohan before the arrival of the Saiyans.
explanation: True. Piccolo trains Gohan for a year in the wilderness. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Vegeta is Gohan's first fighting instructor.
explanation: False. Piccolo trains Gohan first. (Spoiler.)

claim: Future Trunks travels back in time to warn the Z Fighters about the Androids.
explanation: True. Future Trunks arrives from a dark future to warn them about the Androids. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Goten is older than Trunks.
explanation: False. Trunks is slightly older than Goten.

claim: Goten and Trunks combine through the Fusion Dance to form Gotenks.
explanation: True. Their fusion is called Gotenks. (Spoiler: Majin Buu Saga.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Z, Androids 17 and 18 were originally human beings.
explanation: True. Dr. Gero transformed them into cyborgs. (Spoiler.)

claim: Krillin and Android 18 have a daughter named Pan.
explanation: False. Their daughter is Marron. Pan is Gohan and Videl's daughter.

claim: Gohan's wife is Videl, the daughter of Mr. Satan (Hercule).
explanation: True. Videl is the daughter of Hercule and marries Gohan.

claim: Bulma's father is Dr. Gero.
explanation: False. Bulma's father is Dr. Brief. Dr. Gero is the creator of the Androids.

claim: Yamcha's signature technique is the Wolf Fang Fist.
explanation: True. The Wolf Fang Fist is Yamcha's trademark attack.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Wolf Fang Fist

claim: Tien Shinhan's signature technique is the Kamehameha.
explanation: False. Tien is known for the Tri-Beam and the Solar Flare. The Kamehameha belongs to Roshi and Goku.

claim: The Super Saiyan Blue transformation first appears in Dragon Ball Z.
explanation: False. Super Saiyan Blue debuts in Dragon Ball Super (the Resurrection 'F' era onward).

claim: Dragon Ball GT is part of the Dragon Ball Super storyline.
explanation: False. GT is a separate anime series that is not part of the Dragon Ball Super story.

claim: Goku was sent to Earth as a baby with the mission of conquering it.
explanation: True. Baby Kakarot was sent to Earth to conquer it, though his head injury changed his nature. (Spoiler.)

claim: King Vegeta was killed by Goku.
explanation: False. King Vegeta was killed by Frieza. (Spoiler.)

claim: The Final Flash is one of Vegeta's signature techniques.
explanation: True. Vegeta uses Final Flash as a signature energy wave.

claim: Piccolo fuses with the Namekian Nail on the planet Namek.
explanation: True. Piccolo fuses with Nail to gain power against Frieza. (Spoiler: Frieza Saga.)

claim: Piccolo fuses with Kami, the former Guardian of Earth.
explanation: True. Piccolo and Kami merge into one being. (Spoiler.)

claim: Goten first becomes a Super Saiyan as an adult.
explanation: False. Goten becomes a Super Saiyan as a young child in the Majin Buu Saga. (Spoiler.)

claim: Vegeta and Bulma have a daughter named Bulla.
explanation: True. Bulla is the younger child of Vegeta and Bulma. (Spoiler: late Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: The Kamehameha was invented by Goku.
explanation: False. Master Roshi invented the Kamehameha, and Goku learned it from watching him.

claim: Tien Shinhan originally trained under Master Shen of the Crane School.
explanation: True. Tien and Chiaotzu were students of Master Shen before they changed sides.

claim: Yamcha is killed by a self-destructing Saibaman during the Saiyan Saga.
explanation: True. A Saibaman's self-destruct kills Yamcha; he is later revived with the Dragon Balls. (Spoiler.)

claim: Master Roshi's pet turtle is named Oolong.
explanation: False. Oolong is a shape-shifting pig. Roshi's sea turtle companion is simply called Turtle.

claim: The Destructo Disc was invented by Yamcha.
explanation: False. The Destructo Disc is Krillin's signature technique.

claim: Vegeta first becomes a Super Saiyan during the Frieza Saga on Namek.
explanation: False. Vegeta does not achieve Super Saiyan on Namek; he achieves it in the later Androids storyline. (Spoiler.)

claim: Goku defeats Frieza on Namek using Super Saiyan 3.
explanation: False. Goku fights Frieza as a regular Super Saiyan. Super Saiyan 3 appears in the Majin Buu Saga. (Spoiler.)

claim: Gohan defeats Cell by using Super Saiyan 3.
explanation: False. Gohan defeats Cell as a Super Saiyan 2 with a father-son Kamehameha. (Spoiler.)

claim: Frieza is the ruler of an intergalactic empire that conquers planets and sells them.
explanation: True. Frieza leads the Frieza Force, which seizes planets and sells them.

claim: Frieza is a Saiyan.
explanation: False. Frieza belongs to a separate species, not the Saiyans. He is the tyrant who dominated the Saiyans.

claim: Cell absorbs Androids 17 and 18 to reach his Perfect Form.
explanation: True. Cell absorbs 17 and then 18 to reach his Perfect Form. (Spoiler: Cell Saga.)

claim: Cell was created using only Goku's cells.
explanation: False. Cell was created from cells of several fighters, including Goku, Vegeta, Piccolo, Frieza and King Cold. (Spoiler.)

claim: Majin Buu was created by the wizard Bibidi.
explanation: True. Bibidi created Majin Buu long before the Majin Buu Saga. (Spoiler.)

claim: Beerus is a Supreme Kai.
explanation: False. Beerus is the God of Destruction of Universe 7.

claim: Beerus is the God of Destruction of Universe 7.
explanation: True. Beerus holds this role, and Whis is his attendant.

claim: Champa is Beerus's father.
explanation: False. Champa is Beerus's twin brother and the God of Destruction of Universe 6.

claim: Jiren is a member of the Pride Troopers of Universe 11.
explanation: True. Jiren is a Pride Trooper and a top fighter of Universe 11 in Dragon Ball Super.

claim: Zamasu is a Saiyan.
explanation: False. Zamasu is a Supreme Kai in training from Universe 10. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: The Ginyu Force is an elite squad serving Frieza and led by Captain Ginyu.
explanation: True. Captain Ginyu leads Frieza's elite fighting squad. (Spoiler: Frieza Saga.)

claim: Captain Ginyu swaps bodies with Vegeta.
explanation: False. Captain Ginyu swaps bodies with Goku using the Body Change technique. (Spoiler.)

claim: Guldo of the Ginyu Force can stop time for a short period.
explanation: True. Guldo's Time Freeze lets him halt time while he holds his breath. (Spoiler.)

claim: Recoome is the leader of the Ginyu Force.
explanation: False. Captain Ginyu is the leader of the Ginyu Force. (Spoiler.)

claim: Cell's first form is known as Imperfect Cell.
explanation: True. Cell begins as Imperfect Cell, then becomes Semi-Perfect, then Perfect. (Spoiler.)

claim: Cell reaches his Perfect Form after absorbing only Android 17.
explanation: False. Absorbing 17 makes Cell Semi-Perfect; he becomes Perfect only after absorbing 18 as well. (Spoiler.)

claim: Cell announces that the Cell Games will begin ten days after his announcement.
explanation: True. Cell announces the tournament and gives the world time to prepare. (Spoiler.)

claim: Cell creates Cell Juniors during the Cell Games.
explanation: True. Cell Juniors are miniature versions of Cell that fight the Z Fighters. (Spoiler.)

claim: Kid Buu is the original, purest form of Majin Buu.
explanation: True. Kid Buu is the original, purely evil form. (Spoiler: Majin Buu Saga.)

claim: Fat Buu is Majin Buu's original, purest form.
explanation: False. Fat Buu is a gentler form; the original form is Kid Buu. (Spoiler.)

claim: Beerus makes his first appearance in the film Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods.
explanation: True. Beerus debuts in the film Battle of Gods, which leads into Dragon Ball Super. (Movie.)

claim: Champa is the God of Destruction of Universe 7.
explanation: False. Champa is the God of Destruction of Universe 6. Beerus oversees Universe 7.

claim: Golden Frieza debuts in the film Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F'.
explanation: True. Frieza's golden form debuts in that film. (Movie.)

claim: Golden Frieza first appears in the Frieza Saga of the original Dragon Ball Z series.
explanation: False. Golden Frieza appears much later, in the film Resurrection 'F'. (Movie.)

claim: In Resurrection 'F', Frieza is revived by his soldiers Sorbet and Tagoma.
explanation: True. They use the Dragon Balls to bring Frieza back. (Movie spoiler.)

claim: Fused Zamasu is formed through the Fusion Dance.
explanation: False. Fused Zamasu is formed with the Potara earrings. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Goku Black is Zamasu using Goku's body.
explanation: True. Zamasu swaps bodies with Goku to become Goku Black. (Spoiler.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Zamasu's plan is to destroy only the Saiyans.
explanation: False. His 'Zero Mortals' plan aims to wipe out all mortals. (Spoiler.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, the Tournament of Power takes place in the World of Void.
explanation: True. The tournament is held on a special arena in the World of Void. (Spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Tournament of Power

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Universe 6 wins the Tournament of Power.
explanation: False. Universe 7 wins the tournament. (Spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Tournament of Power

claim: Android 17 is the last Universe 7 fighter standing at the end of the Tournament of Power.
explanation: True. Android 17 is the last Universe 7 fighter standing. (Spoiler.)

claim: Hit is a fighter from Universe 7.
explanation: False. Hit is an assassin from Universe 6.

claim: In the film Dragon Ball Super: Broly, Paragus is Broly's father.
explanation: True. In Dragon Ball Super: Broly, Paragus is Broly's father. (Movie.)

claim: Broly appears in the original Dragon Ball manga.
explanation: False. Broly originated in the Dragon Ball Z films, not the original manga. (Movie.)

claim: The Broly of the Dragon Ball Z films is the same continuity as the Broly of the film Dragon Ball Super: Broly.
explanation: False. The 2018 film reintroduces Broly in the Dragon Ball Super continuity and replaces the Z film version. (Movie.)

claim: Cell's body was built using cells from Goku, Vegeta, Piccolo, Frieza and King Cold.
explanation: True. Dr. Gero's creation incorporates cells from these fighters. (Spoiler.)

claim: Cell's body includes cells from Krillin.
explanation: False. Krillin's cells are not part of Cell's makeup. (Spoiler.)

claim: Frieza explains that his lower forms exist to limit his power.
explanation: True. Frieza says his earlier forms hold back his power. (Spoiler.)

claim: Kid Buu is defeated by Gohan.
explanation: False. Kid Buu is defeated by Goku's Spirit Bomb. (Spoiler.)

claim: Kid Buu is defeated by Goku's Spirit Bomb, powered with energy from people on Earth.
explanation: True. Energy lent by the people of Earth powers the Spirit Bomb. (Spoiler.)

claim: Beerus is awakened from his slumber because of Vegeta's fight with Cell.
explanation: False. Beerus awakens because of a prophecy about the Super Saiyan God. (Movie.)

claim: The Super Saiyan God ritual in Battle of Gods requires only three Saiyans.
explanation: False. The ritual requires six righteous Saiyans. (Movie.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Super Saiyan God

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Android 17's original human name is Lapis.
explanation: True. Dragon Ball Super reveals the names Lapis (17) and Lazuli (18).

claim: Dr. Gero was a scientist working for the Red Ribbon Army.
explanation: True. Dr. Gero worked for the Red Ribbon Army before creating the Androids.

claim: Commander Red leads the Red Ribbon Army.
explanation: True. Commander Red is the head of the Red Ribbon Army.

claim: The Red Ribbon Army is defeated by Piccolo.
explanation: False. In the original Dragon Ball, Goku takes down the Red Ribbon Army.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Red Ribbon Army

claim: King Piccolo was sealed using the Evil Containment Wave.
explanation: True. Master Mutaito sealed King Piccolo with the Evil Containment Wave. (Spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Evil Containment Wave

claim: Goku Black first appears in Dragon Ball GT.
explanation: False. Goku Black is a Dragon Ball Super character; GT is a separate continuity.

claim: In Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero, Gamma 1 is a Saiyan.
explanation: False. Gamma 1 is an android created by Dr. Hedo. (Movie.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero, Magenta is Dr. Gero's brother.
explanation: False. Magenta is the son of Commander Red. (Movie.)

claim: A Saiyan with a tail transforms into a Great Ape when exposed to a full moon.
explanation: True. Saiyans with tails turn into Great Apes when they look at a full moon (Blutz waves), as established in the original Dragon Ball and Dragon Ball Z.

claim: In Dragon Ball Z, a Super Saiyan has golden hair and a golden aura.
explanation: True. The Super Saiyan transformation is known for spiky golden hair and a golden aura.

claim: Goku learns Instant Transmission on the planet Yardrat.
explanation: True. Goku picks up the technique from the Yardrats after the Frieza Saga. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Goku learns Instant Transmission from King Kai.
explanation: False. Goku learns Instant Transmission from the Yardrats. King Kai teaches him the Kaioken and the Spirit Bomb.

claim: Goku learns the Kaioken technique from King Kai.
explanation: True. King Kai teaches Goku the Kaioken during his training in the afterlife. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: The Spirit Bomb draws its energy solely from the body of the person who throws it.
explanation: False. The Spirit Bomb gathers energy from living things around the user, which is its defining feature.

claim: In Dragon Ball Z, a fusion created with the Fusion Dance lasts for 30 minutes.
explanation: True. Fusion Dance fusions last thirty minutes before the fused warriors separate again.

claim: The Fusion Dance works between any two fighters regardless of their size or power difference.
explanation: False. The Fusion Dance requires two fighters of similar height and power levels, and the movements must be performed in sync.

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Ultra Instinct is a state in which the body moves and reacts on its own, without conscious thought.
explanation: True. Ultra Instinct lets the user's body react to attacks automatically. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super, Tournament of Power.)

claim: Ultra Instinct first appears in the original Dragon Ball Z series.
explanation: False. Ultra Instinct debuts in Dragon Ball Super, not in Dragon Ball Z.

claim: The Kaioken multiplies the user's power, but it strains the user's body.
explanation: True. Higher Kaioken multipliers put greater strain on the user's body.

claim: Super Saiyan God and Super Saiyan Blue are the same transformation.
explanation: False. Super Saiyan God is a distinct transformation using god ki. Super Saiyan Blue is a Super Saiyan form powered by god ki. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Super Saiyan Blue

claim: The Super Saiyan God transformation debuts in the film Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods.
explanation: True. Goku first becomes Super Saiyan God in Battle of Gods. (Movie spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Super Saiyan God

claim: Gohan unlocks his latent potential through a ritual performed by the Elder Kai.
explanation: True. The Elder Kai's ritual unlocks Gohan's hidden power, giving rise to the form often called Ultimate (Mystic) Gohan. (Spoiler: Majin Buu Saga.)

claim: Gotenks is formed using Potara earrings.
explanation: False. Gotenks is created by Goten and Trunks performing the Fusion Dance. (Spoiler: Majin Buu Saga.)

claim: Vegito is formed using Potara earrings, while Gogeta is formed using the Fusion Dance.
explanation: True. In Dragon Ball Z, Goku and Vegeta form Vegito with the Potara and Gogeta (in the film Fusion Reborn) with the Fusion Dance. (Spoiler.)

claim: Super Saiyan 4 appears in Dragon Ball Super.
explanation: False. Super Saiyan 4 belongs to Dragon Ball GT, which is a separate continuity from Dragon Ball Super.

claim: The Special Beam Cannon is Piccolo's signature technique.
explanation: True. Piccolo invented and uses the Special Beam Cannon (Makankosappo), a drilling beam attack.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Special Beam Cannon

claim: The Special Beam Cannon is a technique invented by a Saiyan.
explanation: False. The Special Beam Cannon is Piccolo's Namekian technique.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Special Beam Cannon

claim: A Saiyan who recovers from a near-death injury becomes stronger through the Zenkai boost.
explanation: True. The Zenkai boost is a Saiyan trait that increases power after recovering from serious injury.

claim: Instant Transmission lets the user teleport anywhere without needing to sense a ki signature.
explanation: False. The user must lock onto a ki signature to teleport to that location.

claim: Namekians can regenerate lost limbs.
explanation: True. Namekians are known for regenerating lost body parts.

claim: A Saiyan's tail has no weakness, and grabbing it has no effect.
explanation: False. A Saiyan's tail is a notable weakness; grabbing it can weaken the Saiyan unless the weakness has been trained away.

claim: In Dragon Ball Z, Dr. Gero's Androids 17 and 18 have no ki that can be sensed.
explanation: True. Their energy cannot be sensed like a normal fighter's. (Spoiler: Android Saga.)

claim: A Saiyan can only become a Super Saiyan while looking at a full moon.
explanation: False. The Great Ape form is triggered by the full moon. The Super Saiyan transformation is triggered by emotion and power.

claim: Vegeta's Ultra Ego form appears in Dragon Ball Super.
explanation: True. Ultra Ego is Vegeta's god-of-destruction-style power in Dragon Ball Super, which grows stronger as he takes damage. (Spoiler: Granolah arc, manga.)

claim: Ascended Super Saiyan is another name for Super Saiyan 2.
explanation: False. Ascended Super Saiyan is a separate, bulkier Super Saiyan variant. Super Saiyan 2 is its own transformation.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Ascended Super Saiyan

claim: The Golden Great Ape appears in Dragon Ball GT.
explanation: True. Golden Great Apes appear in Dragon Ball GT as a step toward Super Saiyan 4. (GT continuity.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Golden Great Ape

claim: Ultra Instinct Sign and Mastered Ultra Instinct are the same form.
explanation: False. Ultra Instinct Sign is an incomplete, unstable state. Mastered Ultra Instinct is the complete form with silver hair. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: Super Saiyan Rosé is a transformation associated with Goku Black.
explanation: True. Goku Black uses Super Saiyan Rosé in Dragon Ball Super. (Spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Super Saiyan Rosé

claim: Goku first uses the Spirit Bomb against Cell.
explanation: False. Goku's first Spirit Bomb in Dragon Ball Z is used against Vegeta. (Spoiler: Saiyan Saga.)

claim: Goku uses the Kaioken against Vegeta during the Saiyan Saga.
explanation: True. Goku uses the Kaioken, at increasing multipliers, in his battle with Vegeta. (Spoiler.)

claim: Jiren uses Ultra Instinct during the Tournament of Power.
explanation: False. Goku is the fighter who uses Ultra Instinct against Jiren. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: Goku first uses Ultra Instinct (Sign) in his fight against Jiren during the Tournament of Power.
explanation: True. Goku first displays the Ultra Instinct state against Jiren. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: A user of Instant Transmission can take other people along by having them touch the user.
explanation: True. Goku can carry others with him when they make contact.

claim: Hakai is a destruction technique associated with the Gods of Destruction.
explanation: True. Hakai is the signature destruction power of the Gods of Destruction, such as Beerus. (Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: A Namekian can reproduce by spitting out an egg.
explanation: True. Namekians reproduce asexually by laying an egg, as shown with King Piccolo and Piccolo.

claim: Gotenks can reach the Super Saiyan 3 form.
explanation: True. Gotenks reaches Super Saiyan 3 during the Majin Buu Saga. (Spoiler.)

claim: The Galick Gun is one of Vegeta's signature energy attacks.
explanation: True. Vegeta uses the Galick Gun from the Saiyan Saga onward.

claim: The power-up Gohan receives from the Elder Kai is often called Mystic Gohan.
explanation: True. The form is known as Ultimate Gohan and also as Mystic Gohan. (Spoiler: Majin Buu Saga.)

claim: Instant Transmission can only be used while the user is in a Super Saiyan form.
explanation: False. Instant Transmission is not tied to any transformation.

claim: Super Saiyan 2 first appears during the Frieza Saga.
explanation: False. Super Saiyan 2 first appears later, during the Cell Saga. (Spoiler.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Vegito Blue is formed through the Fusion Dance.
explanation: False. Vegito is formed with Potara earrings. The Fusion Dance creates Gogeta. (Spoiler.)

claim: Vegeta learned the Final Flash from Piccolo.
explanation: False. Final Flash is Vegeta's own technique, not one taught by Piccolo.

claim: Saiyans in Great Ape form always retain full control of their mind.
explanation: False. Great Apes typically lose rational control unless they have trained to control the form.

claim: Super Saiyan Rosé is a transformation achieved by Vegeta.
explanation: False. Super Saiyan Rosé is the form of Goku Black, not Vegeta. (Spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Super Saiyan Rosé

claim: Vegeta is trained in Ultra Ego by Whis.
explanation: False. In the Dragon Ball Super manga, Beerus trains Vegeta in Ultra Ego. (Spoiler: Granolah arc.)

claim: Namekians are unable to sense ki.
explanation: False. Namekians such as Piccolo can sense ki.

claim: A Saiyan's tail can never regrow once it has been cut off.
explanation: False. Saiyan tails can regrow after being cut, unless the Saiyan permanently removes them.

claim: Instant Transmission can be used to travel through time.
explanation: False. Instant Transmission is a teleportation technique and does not allow time travel.

claim: Earth's seven Dragon Balls must be gathered to summon the dragon Shenron.
explanation: True. Gathering all seven of Earth's Dragon Balls summons Shenron, who grants a wish.

claim: Shenron is the dragon summoned by the Dragon Balls of Namek.
explanation: False. Namek's Dragon Balls summon Porunga. Shenron is the dragon of Earth's Dragon Balls.

claim: In the original Dragon Ball, Goku's keepsake from his grandfather Gohan is the four-star Dragon Ball.
explanation: True. Goku's four-star ball is the keepsake from his grandfather and is what draws Bulma to him at the start of the story.

claim: Kami grows the Senzu Beans that heal fighters in Dragon Ball.
explanation: False. Korin, the cat sage of Korin Tower, grows the Senzu Beans.

claim: Bulma invents the Dragon Radar, which locates Dragon Balls.
explanation: True. Bulma builds the Dragon Radar to track down the Dragon Balls.

claim: Kami created Earth's Dragon Balls.
explanation: True. Kami, the Guardian of Earth, created them. (Spoiler: later Dragon Ball Z lore.)

claim: Dende, who later becomes the Guardian of Earth, is a Saiyan.
explanation: False. Dende is a Namekian from the planet Namek. (Spoiler.)

claim: In the original Dragon Ball, Emperor Pilaf seeks the Dragon Balls in order to rule the world.
explanation: True. Pilaf's goal is to collect the Dragon Balls and use the wish to rule the world.

claim: In the original Dragon Ball, Emperor Pilaf successfully makes his wish for world domination with Shenron.
explanation: False. Pilaf is interrupted when Oolong makes a wish first. Shenron grants only one wish. (Spoiler: early original Dragon Ball.)

claim: Master Roshi trains both Goku and Krillin in the original Dragon Ball.
explanation: True. Roshi takes Goku and Krillin on as students.

claim: Porunga, the dragon of Namek's Dragon Balls, can grant three wishes.
explanation: True. Porunga grants up to three wishes. (Spoiler: Frieza Saga.)

claim: After a wish is granted, Earth's original Dragon Balls scatter and turn to stone for a time.
explanation: True. The Dragon Balls scatter and become inactive for about a year before they can be used again.

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, the Super Dragon Balls belong to Universe 7.
explanation: False. The Super Dragon Balls belong to Universe 6.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Super Dragon Balls

claim: In the Hyperbolic Time Chamber, one day outside equals one year inside.
explanation: True. A day outside corresponds to a year inside the chamber.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Hyperbolic Time Chamber

claim: The Hyperbolic Time Chamber is located on King Kai's planet.
explanation: False. It is a room at Kami's Lookout above the Earth.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Hyperbolic Time Chamber

claim: Kami is the good half of a Namekian who separated from his evil half, King Piccolo.
explanation: True. Kami and King Piccolo are the two halves of one Namekian. (Spoiler.)

claim: Dende is a Namekian with the power to heal others.
explanation: True. Dende's healing ability is first seen on Namek. (Spoiler: Frieza Saga.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, the Supreme Kai Shin is Beerus's attendant.
explanation: False. Beerus's attendant is the Angel Whis. Shin is a Supreme Kai.

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Whis is the son of the Grand Priest.
explanation: True. The Grand Priest is Whis's father. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, the Grand Priest is the ruler of all universes.
explanation: False. The ruler of all universes is the Omni-King, Zeno. The Grand Priest serves Zeno.

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Omni-King Zeno can erase entire universes.
explanation: True. Zeno can erase universes, as established in the Future Trunks and Tournament of Power arcs. (Spoiler.)

claim: All twelve universes take part in the Tournament of Power.
explanation: False. Eight universes take part in the Tournament of Power. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Tournament of Power

claim: The Tournament of Power lasts 48 minutes.
explanation: True. The tournament has a 48-minute time limit. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Tournament of Power

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Frieza fights on Universe 7's team in the Tournament of Power.
explanation: True. Frieza joins Universe 7's team. (Spoiler.)

claim: In Future Trunks's timeline, the time machine was built by Dr. Brief.
explanation: False. Future Bulma built the time machine. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: In Future Trunks's timeline, Goku died of a heart virus.
explanation: True. In that timeline Goku died of the heart virus before the Androids' rampage. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Z.)

claim: Goku sacrifices himself by teleporting Cell to King Kai's planet.
explanation: True. Goku teleports Cell there to stop his self-destruction. (Spoiler: Cell Saga.)

claim: Hercule (Mr. Satan) truly defeats Cell in the Cell Games.
explanation: False. The world believes Hercule did it, but Gohan defeats Cell. (Spoiler.)

claim: In the film Dragon Ball Super: Broly, Planet Vegeta was originally called Planet Sadala.
explanation: True. The film explains that the Saiyans' homeworld was originally named Planet Sadala. (Movie.)

claim: Namek's Dragon Balls were created by Kami.
explanation: False. Namek's Dragon Balls were created by Grand Elder Guru. Kami created Earth's. (Spoiler.)

claim: Goku defeats Piccolo Jr. in the 23rd World Martial Arts Tournament.
explanation: True. Goku defeats Piccolo Jr. in the 23rd tournament. (Spoiler: original Dragon Ball.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - World Martial Arts Tournament

claim: Goku wins the 21st World Martial Arts Tournament.
explanation: False. Goku loses the 21st tournament to Jackie Chun (Master Roshi in disguise). He wins the 23rd. (Spoiler.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - World Martial Arts Tournament

claim: In Dragon Ball GT, Goku is turned into a child by a wish made by Emperor Pilaf with the Black Star Dragon Balls.
explanation: True in GT continuity. Pilaf's wish turns Goku back into a child. (GT only.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Black Star Dragon Balls

claim: In Dragon Ball GT, Goku is turned into a child by a wish made by Garlic Jr.
explanation: False. In GT, Emperor Pilaf makes the wish. (GT only.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Black Star Dragon Balls

claim: In Dragon Ball GT, the Black Star Dragon Balls scatter across space, and Earth will explode if they are not gathered within a year.
explanation: True in GT continuity. The Black Star Dragon Balls scatter across the galaxy after the wish. (GT only.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Black Star Dragon Balls

claim: The Black Star Dragon Balls first appear in Dragon Ball Super.
explanation: False. The Black Star Dragon Balls belong to Dragon Ball GT, a separate continuity from Super.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Black Star Dragon Balls

claim: In Dragon Ball GT, overuse of the Dragon Balls gives rise to the Shadow Dragons.
explanation: True in GT. Negative energy built up through repeated wishes leads to the Shadow Dragons. (GT only.)

claim: In Dragon Ball GT, the villain Baby is a Saiyan.
explanation: False. Baby is a Tuffle parasite who takes over hosts, such as Vegeta. (GT only.)

claim: Dragon Ball DAIMA takes place mainly in the Demon Realm.
explanation: True. DAIMA (2024) is set largely in the Demon Realm.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Dragon Ball DAIMA

claim: In Dragon Ball DAIMA, Goku and his friends are turned into children.
explanation: True. The cast is turned into children at the start of DAIMA. (DAIMA only.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Dragon Ball DAIMA

claim: Dragon Ball DAIMA is a sequel to Dragon Ball GT.
explanation: False. DAIMA is not a continuation of GT; it belongs to the main Dragon Ball continuity, between the Majin Buu saga and Super.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Dragon Ball DAIMA

claim: In Dragon Ball Super, Whis is a God of Destruction.
explanation: False. Whis is an Angel, the attendant of Beerus, not a God of Destruction.

claim: Dragon Ball Super establishes that there are twelve universes.
explanation: True. Dragon Ball Super establishes twelve universes, each with a God of Destruction.

claim: Goku's first World Martial Arts Tournament is the 22nd.
explanation: False. Goku first enters the 21st tournament. (Spoiler: original Dragon Ball.)
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - World Martial Arts Tournament

claim: Shenron revives Goku after his sacrifice in the Cell Saga.
explanation: False. Goku stays dead after the Cell Games and is not revived until later. (Spoiler.)

claim: Beerus is awakened in Dragon Ball GT.
explanation: False. Beerus awakens in Battle of Gods and Dragon Ball Super. GT is a separate continuity.

claim: Piccolo is Kami's son.
explanation: False. Piccolo is not Kami's son; he is the reincarnation of King Piccolo, Kami's evil half. (Spoiler.)

claim: Future Zeno is Zeno's twin brother.
explanation: False. Future Zeno is the future version of Zeno from another time. (Spoiler: Dragon Ball Super.)

claim: In Dragon Ball DAIMA, Majin Buu is the main antagonist.
explanation: False. DAIMA's main antagonist is Gomah, not Majin Buu.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Dragon Ball DAIMA

claim: Dragon Ball DAIMA is set in Universe 6.
explanation: False. DAIMA takes place in Goku's own universe, Universe 7, in the Demon Realm.
source_name: Dragon Ball Wiki - Dragon Ball DAIMA
